subject.title: Org claim: vmware-aiops + vmware-monitor — @kingaiwork lookalikes impersonate @zw008 listings (same pattern as #2966/#3035)

question: After confirming the audited resolution of both VMware listings, should staff limit enforcement to these records or apply account-level action for the repeated @kingaiwork impersonation pattern?
rationale: The listing-level remedy is supported by the existing workflow, but banning the publisher affects every owned skill, token, comment, and account state and requires authorized human judgment.

options.title: Verify listings, review account
options.body: Confirm both report outcomes and install recovery, then perform a scoped account review using the two earlier same-pattern claims before choosing broader enforcement.

options.title: Resolve listings only
options.body: Close after both listings and audit entries are verified, leaving the publisher active unless a separate case establishes account-wide abuse.

options.title: Apply account enforcement
options.body: Ban or otherwise restrict the publisher if authorized review confirms that the repeated pattern meets the account-level abuse threshold.

recommendation.title: Verify listings, review account
recommendation.body: Confirm both report outcomes and install recovery, then perform a scoped account review using the two earlier same-pattern claims before choosing broader enforcement.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick is the strongest routing candidate from the merged claim-intake work, namespace RFC, and recent moderation-path history.
